title: The Evil Quartet & Recent Extinctions
topic: IUCN 784 Recent Extinctions, Habitat Loss, Over-Exploitation, & The Evil Quartet Framework
quickSummary: Biodiversity loss & extinction dynamics: IUCN Red List (2004) documents the extinction of 784 species in the last 500 years (338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates, 87 plants). Recent classic extinctions: Dodo (Mauritius), Quagga (Africa), Thylacine / Tasmanian Tiger (Australia), Steller's Sea Cow (Russia), and three subspecies of tiger (Bali, Javan, Caspian). The 'Evil Quartet' (Jared Diamond): (1) Habitat Loss & Fragmentation (the single most important driver; Amazon cleared for soy/cattle); (2) Over-Exploitation (greed driving Steller's Sea Cow & Passenger Pigeon to extinction); (3) Alien Species Invasions; (4) Co-Extinctions.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 5.1 The Modern Anthropogenic Extinction Crisis
- The **IUCN Red List (2004)** records that **$784\text{ species}$ have become completely extinct within the last $500\text{ years}$**:
  - **$338\text{ Vertebrates}$**
  - **$359\text{ Invertebrates}$**
  - **$87\text{ Plants}$**
- **Recent Famous Extinction Case Studies**:
  - **Dodo (*Raphus cucullatus*)** $\longrightarrow$ Island of **Mauritius** (flightless pigeon preyed on by sailors & pigs).
  - **Quagga (*Equus quagga*)** $\longrightarrow$ **South Africa** (over-hunted zebra subspecies).
  - **Thylacine (Tasmanian Tiger / Wolf)** $\longrightarrow$ **Tasmania / Australia**.
  - **Steller’s Sea Cow (*Hydrodamalis gigas*)** $\longrightarrow$ **Russia / Bering Sea** (hunted to extinction in 27 years).
  - **Three Subspecies of Tiger (*Panthera tigris*)** $\longrightarrow$ **Bali, Javan, and Caspian tigers**.

### 5.2 The 'Evil Quartet' — Driver 1: Habitat Loss & Fragmentation
- **The single most important and devastating cause** of animal and plant extinctions worldwide.
- **Tropical Rainforest Deforestation**:
  - Tropical rainforests once covered $>14\%$ of the Earth’s total land surface; today, they cover **less than $6\%$**.
  - **The Amazon Rainforest** is being systematically cleared and incinerated at alarming rates for cultivating **Soybeans** and converting tracts into **Beef Cattle pastures**.
- **Habitat Fragmentation**:
  - When large, continuous forest tracts are broken into small fragmented patches by highways, agriculture, and urban sprawl, mammals and birds requiring large home ranges and animals with migratory habits suffer catastrophic population collapses.

### 5.3 The 'Evil Quartet' — Driver 2: Over-Exploitation
- Humans have always depended on biological nature for food and shelter. However, when economic **need turns to commercial greed**, it leads to over-exploitation of natural populations.
- Over-harvesting directly drove **Steller's Sea Cow** and the **Passenger Pigeon (*Ectopistes migratorius*)** to total extinction within recent historical times.
- Today, excessive commercial overfishing severely threatens global marine fish stocks.

conceptBreakdown.heading: The Sixth Mass Extinction (Anthropocene)
conceptBreakdown.title: The Sixth Mass Extinction (Anthropocene)
conceptBreakdown.content: Earth has experienced five previous mass extinction episodes over geological time (e.g., End-Cretaceous asteroid impact); the current ongoing Sixth Extinction is entirely anthropogenic and proceeding 100 to 1,000 times faster than natural background extinction rates.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Vulnerability to Extinction Traits
conceptBreakdown.title: Vulnerability to Extinction Traits
conceptBreakdown.content: Species with large body size, high trophic positions, low reproductive potential (low r), narrow geographic distribution, high endemism, and fixed migratory corridors are most susceptible to extinction.
